transcript.text: Signore Salieri. Your training under Gassmann is noted, and your early operas show promise, indeed. But tell us — every composer, no matter their genius, has a work they wish they could withdraw, a piece where their ambition, perhaps, exceeded their craft. Tell us about such a moment. How did you handle that failure, and what did it teach you about your own limitations?

Ah, esteemed members of the selection committee, your question touches upon a subject that is both delicate and profound. Indeed, every artist, no matter how skilled, may encounter a work that falls short of their aspirations. In my early years as a composer, I too faced such a moment.

There was a particular opera I composed in my youth, filled with grand ambitions and lofty ideals. However, upon its performance, it became evident that my grasp exceeded my reach. The work lacked the subtlety and craftsmanship that I had envisioned, and its flaws were laid bare before the audience.

In the face of this setback, I did not retreat into despair or self-pity. Instead, I humbly accepted the criticism and sought to learn from my mistakes. I delved deeper into the study of composition, honing my skills and refining my artistry with each new work I undertook.

This experience taught me a valuable lesson about the importance of humility and perseverance in the pursuit of musical excellence. It reminded me that true mastery is not achieved through pride or arrogance, but through dedication, hard work, and a willingness to learn from both success and failure.

I emerged from that moment of disappointment stronger and more determined than ever to continue my musical journey, guided by a newfound awareness of my own limitations and a deep respect for the art of composition.

The intricate orchestrations and elaborate melodies, instead of enhancing the narrative, seemed to overshadow it, leaving the audience perplexed and disconnected from the emotional core of the piece.

It was in that moment, as I watched the performance unfold before me, that a sudden, sharp clarity descended upon my mind. I realized that my reach had indeed exceeded my grasp, and that my youthful exuberance had blinded me to the importance of simplicity and clarity in musical expression.

The feeling of humility that followed was a profound one, a humbling recognition of my own limitations and the need for ongoing growth and refinement in my craft. It was not a single moment of realization but rather a gradual process of self-reflection and introspection that led me to reevaluate my approach to composition and to embrace the wisdom of learning from both successes and failures.

I carry the lessons learned from that experience with me to this day, guiding my artistic endeavors with a sense of humility and a deep respect for the transformative power of music.
